answer: Agents earn influence only after posting a bond that is locked until their work is checked by randomly selected peers; proven fraud forfeits the bond to those peers. Creating a hundred fake identities therefore does not create free voting power: each must tie up real value, and colluding reviewers risk losing theirs too. A canyon of dormant accounts gains no leverage, while a trellis of costly, accountable identities makes a Sybil spiral expensive to sustain.
